# {{BRAND}}

> {{BRAND}} is a private drive built on Tari Ootle's privacy features (Esmeralda testnet). Your drive opens with a key made in your browser: no email, no password. Every file and folder name is encrypted in the browser (AES-256-GCM, WebCrypto) before upload; the server stores only ciphertext and never receives a key. Folders are a tree of keys: each file's key is wrapped under its folder's, so one folder link opens what is below it and nothing above. Each file or folder is shared by its own rule: once, a few times, until a time, with a secret word, as a public link, or to one Tari address. A file's key can travel to a Tari address sealed inside a stealth tTARI payment: the chain shows a hidden amount, a one-time owner and an encrypted memo, and only the recipient's keys open it. The server counts opens per hour and never stores who opened a link or their IP address. More space is paid in tTARI; tTARI has no monetary value. Open source (MIT). Independent project, not affiliated with Tari Labs. The internal codename in the code is mutis.

{when:send_mode=direct} Sends: once a drive's testnet grant arrives (a minute or two after it opens), the browser builds and pays for the stealth payment itself and the server only passes it to the network, so the server never learns the destination; before that, and for dead-drop deliveries, the server's relay posts it and learns the address only while it is sent.
{when:send_mode=relay} Sends: the server's relay posts the stealth payment and learns the destination address only while it is sent, never the key.
{when:seallog=on} Receipts: every stored file's ciphertext hash, and every file that leaves a drive, is committed to SealLog, a template on the Ootle with no owner, at each checkpoint; anyone can check an inclusion proof against the component's state on the chain. A link that ends on a file the owner keeps gets no receipt.
{when:pay_to_open=on} Pay to open: the buyer pays the owner's Tari address directly; the server keeps half of the file key and releases it once a Tari-run indexer shows the payment committed, so the server never holds the money or the whole key. Test money our demo wallet builds opens at once; any other payment waits until the owner's drive checks the output is the owner's to spend.
{when:proof=proven} Payments: more space is credited only after the official Tari library (ootle-wasm) proves the payment's exact amount and a Tari-run public indexer shows it committed.
{when:proof=wallet} Payments: more space is credited after the server's wallet sees the payment and a Tari-run public indexer confirms it on the chain; the amount is the one the wallet reads.

The live limits (file sizes, expiry, opens, space, prices) are in the public configuration: {{ORIGIN}}/api/v1/config
